title: Borsuk's conjecture fails in dimension nine
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's theorem (2026) that the compact set of rank-one orthogonal projections of R^4, a copy of real projective three-space in the nine-dimensional space of trace-one symmetric matrices, cannot be covered by ten subsets of smaller diameter, so Borsuk's conjecture fails in dimension nine and in every higher dimension. The first lesson turns a cover into an admissible map from projective space to a simplex. The second proves Sard's theorem, regular level sets and degree modulo two with local counting. The third proves the transfer sequence of a double cover, the homology of projective spaces, the Borsuk-Ulam theorem and a degree-zero statement for products. The fourth extends an admissible map to an odd map between spheres of symmetric matrices and of l1-vectors. The fifth shows that with the minimal number of labels the supports form a pure complex whose facets give a cycle modulo two. The sixth rules out ten labels on R^4 by the combinatorics of six-label triangle systems and completes the proof.
prerequisites: core course Algebraic Topology (D60): Fomberg's notes, Theorems 1.13, 1.21, 1.23, Corollaries 1.14, 1.17, Proposition 1.32 (simplicial and singular homology); Roberts's notes, Proposition 8 and Corollary 7 (covering spaces)
core course Real Analysis I (C10): Lebl, Basic Analysis I, Theorem 4.3.2 (Taylor)
core course Measure and Integration (D10): Fremlin, Measure Theory, Vol. 1, 115C-115G, 123C, 123D; Vol. 2, 251N, 252B, 252D, 263A
core course Point-Set Topology (C90): a continuous bijection from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is a homeomorphism
Orientations and fundamental classes (course poincare-duality-on-manifolds): Lemmas 1.1 and 1.2, Proposition 2.3(2), Proposition 3.2, Theorem 4.1, Corollary 5.1
Local tools for bundles and transport (course DG-FND): Lemma 0.4, Theorem 1.2, Corollary 1.3, Theorem 3.1

checks.exact_checks: Python (scratch b9_checks.py and b9_sat.py, outputs b9_checks.out and b9_sat.out, 9 Oct 2026, 0 problems): the projector distance formula and the Euclidean coordinates of trace-one 4x4 matrices on random samples; the circle X_2; the derivative of the matrix square root at I; all six-label triangle systems enumerated (exactly 12) with every property of Lemma 1.3 checked on each, and the list of exercise 4.1; mod 2 Betti numbers (1,1,1) of the six-vertex projective plane and its facet cycle; the Gram vectors of Corollary 3.2. SAT (pycosat): the combinatorial hypotheses of the ten-label argument (purity, even numbers of tetrahedra on triangles, six-label systems on all facet complements) are unsatisfiable; controls: the six-label analogue has exactly the 6 triangle systems through a fixed triangle as solutions, the parity condition alone is satisfiable, the complement-system clauses accept a triangle system and reject perturbations. The complement-system condition alone is already unsatisfiable.
checks.lint: b9_lint.py and b9_bs_scan.py (scratch): headings, provenance line, balanced TeX delimiters, every sibling and course link resolved, no backslash artefacts or control characters; flagged labels are references to other lessons and courses.
checks.source_reading: OpenAI preprint 'A nine-dimensional counterexample to Borsuk's covering assertion' (23 Sep 2026), TeX read in full (introduction, geometry, extension, topology, six-labels, ten-labels, conclusion; library copy openai-math-20261006); every step rederived. Differences: the extension averages against the Gaussian measure instead of the sphere (no uniqueness of invariant measures needed, no dimension factor); the degree-zero step uses the transfer exact sequence instead of Stiefel-Whitney classes and the cohomology ring; Sard's theorem, the Borsuk-Ulam theorem and the homology of projective spaces are proved in the course. Fomberg's and Roberts's notes (core course D60) read for the cited statements; Fremlin 252D and 123C/D and Lebl 4.3.2 checked. Kahn-Kalai, Bondarenko, Conway-Hardin-Sloane, Kalai (arXiv), Jenrich-Brouwer (EJC, open) and Grinsztajn (author's repository) cited by free versions; Hatcher (author's page) cited for context; Borsuk, Perkal, Eggleston, Nilli, Raigorodskii, Hinrichs, Pikhurko, Hinrichs-Richter, Walkup and Arnoux-Marin not cited.
